This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 14.10.2022 at about 6.45 p.m. he had been riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-K-4159 at Heggadihalli, Tubgere Hobli, Doddaballapur Taluk,
Bengaluru District, at that time, another motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-W-7506 ridden by its rider came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motor cycle of the petitioner, as a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
petitioner was taken to Government Hospital, Doddaballapur, after first aid shifted to Ramaiah Medical College Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medicine and Rs.50,000/- towards incidental expenses.
3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 40 years, hale and healthy, working as labour contractor, SCCH-5
thereby
earning Rs.25,000/- p.m., due to this accident he could not attend to his work, undergone untold mental shock and agony.

Out of this accident crime No.259/2022 is registered against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-W-7506 before the Doddaballapur Rural Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is owner of the said motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and submitted that, tribunals is under statutory obligation to sent notices to owners and drivers of the vehicles involved in SCCH-5 the accident.
There is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further admitted issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-7506 and if there is any liability, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denies the occurred of the alleged accident involving the said motor cycle.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
Respondent No.2/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1 and marked 17 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, one witness by name Chandan B. is examined as RW-1, Legal Manager of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-2 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed his evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
SCCH-5 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of vehicle seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.9.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 14.10.2022 at about 6.45 p.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-K-4159 at Heggadihalli,
Tubgere Hobli, Doddaballapur Taluk, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-W-7506.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the SCCH-5 above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 40 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.15, wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner as 1982 and the alleged accident was occurred in the year 2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.15 his age is considered about 40 years as on the date of accident.
Further he was working as Labour Contractor and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

13. As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained right 2nd distal phalanx fracture of right foot CLW in the web space of right foot, for which, he underwent operation in the form of CRIF + K wire+ SCCH-5 wound debridement.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.8, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10 issued by M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, wherein he took treatment from 15.10.2022 to 18.10.2022.

Further he has furnished medical bills amounting to Rs.62,592/- marked as Ex.P.11, advance receipts marked as Ex.P.12, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.13, photos marked as Ex.P.14, X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.17.
14.
Petitioner has not examined the Doctor who has treated him nor produced the disability certificate towards the injuries sustained by hin in the alleged accident.

but on perusal of the facts,
wound certificate and evidence of PW-1 corroborated to believe the injuries sustained by the petitioner out of the accident.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for global compensation SCCH-5 of Rs.75,000/- along with medical bills of Rs.62,592/-, totally a sum of Rs.1,37,592/-, because as per the charge sheet and wound certificate, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and further as per the discharge summary i.e., Ex.P.10 has has taken treatment as inpatient by admitting at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital from 15.10.2022 to 18.10.2022 i.e., he has admitted for 3 days, for the said period he is entitled for compensation as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru.
